lines.text: Recruit, Dr. Hale here. Welcome to the DeusEdix training wing.
I'm in the booth behind the glass, up on your left. Yes, I can see you. That's rather the point.
Everything here was built in the editor a few minutes ago, on your own machine. Walk the rooms and inspect your work.
Room one, the stores. The crate you moved, and the one you placed on top of the crate stockpile platform.
Every object of the game is one click away in the palette. The quartermaster would weep with joy.
Room two. Use the button.
The door opens because you told it to: when JC uses the button, open the door. No tags, no events, no code.
My colleagues behind the glass built doors for twenty years. They are pretending not to be impressed.
Room three. The trooper greets you with the gesture you picked in his properties.
My colleague on the sideline has her own gesture. She calls it supervising. We call it stretching.
Room four. Talk to my colleague: she says what you wrote for her in the Story panel.
If she says anything you didn't write, report it to me at once. Then walk calmly to the exit.
Last room, the library. The books hold the tips that did not fit in a lesson.
That concludes the training, agent. Good work.
I'll file the report now, before anyone asks what we spent on coffee this quarter.
Room five. My smiling crate and your response.
Change the plain crate's skin in the Texture Editor. I expect restraint, legibility, and very little competition.
The committee called mine approachable. They were referring to the crate.
The film stage. Use the screening button to play the shot you made.
The last cup of coffee in this facility, under armed protection. This is a training scenario. Mostly.
When the film ends, carry on to the library. Please leave the principal actor on its pedestal.
